node.statement: Quantitative and C^1 dependence. Substituting H=g_V(P) in node 1.2.1 and using F(P,g_V(P))=0 gives ||g_V(P)+q/2||<=64(e delta+delta^2); node 1.2.2 directly gives the normal derivative estimate. For P_1,P_2, the lower Lipschitz inequality in lem-stage1-quantitative-inverse-function for h↦F(P_1,h), followed by integration of ||D_PF||<=c along the segment from P_1 to P_2, gives (1-c)||g_V(P_1)-g_V(P_2)||<=c||P_1-P_2||. Thus g_V is locally Lipschitz. Expanding the polynomial F at (P,g_V(P)) and using that Lipschitz bound shows that its Frechet derivative is Dg_V(P)=-(D_HF(P,g_V(P)))^(-1)D_PF(P,g_V(P)). The Neumann bound is ||(D_HF)^(-1)||<=1/(1-c), so ||Dg_V(P)||<=c/(1-c)<=2c=128s. Continuity of DF, of g_V, and of inversion on invertible operators makes Dg_V continuous; hence g_V is C^1.
